data.body_html:
Cabopino, a quiet coastal enclave just east of Marbella, hides some of the Costa del Sol's best snorkeling coves. Accessible only by boat, these spots offer clear water, rocky reefs, and a fraction of the crowds found at Marbella's main beaches. This guide provides a marbella boat rental cabopino snorkeling spots map and practical advice for your day on the water.

Why Cabopino for Snorkeling?

Cabopino's coastline is less developed than Marbella's Golden Mile, meaning cleaner water and more natural seabed. The area features two main coves: Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés, plus the sandy stretch of Cabopino Beach. The water is typically calm in summer, with visibility often exceeding 10 metres. The seabed combines sand, seagrass meadows (Posidonia oceanica), and rocky outcrops—perfect for spotting marine life.

From Puerto Banús, it's a 20-minute cruise east. Our [boat rental marbella](/fleet/) fleet includes 18 vessels, from the nimble Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) to the spacious Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax). For a snorkeling-focused trip, the Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) offer a good balance of agility and comfort.

Cabopino Snorkeling Spots Map

Below is a quick-reference map of the three key locations. All are within a short boat ride from each other.

SpotDistance from Puerto BanúsDepthBest for
Cala del Faro15 km (20 min)2-6 mRocky reef, fish
Cala Cortés16 km (22 min)1-4 mBeginners, families
Cabopino Beach14 km (18 min)1-3 mSeagrass meadows, rays

All spots are within 2 km of Cabopino Marina. Your skipper will anchor in sandy patches to avoid damaging the protected seagrass.

How to Book a Boat for Snorkeling

Booking is straightforward. Choose your boat from our fleet—the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are Tier A options at €749 for 2 hours, including skipper, drinks, and snacks. For larger groups, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) starts at €4,719 for 4 hours and includes a jet ski.

All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). Just bring your swimwear, sunscreen, and a towel. We provide masks, snorkels, and fins on request.

What to Expect at Each Spot

Cala del Faro

This cove sits beneath the Cabopino lighthouse. The seabed is mostly rock with crevices where fish hide. Expect to see salema, bream, and damselfish. The water is clear but can be slightly cooler due to currents. Best visited in the morning when the sun lights up the reef.

Cala Cortés

A sheltered sandy cove with shallow water—ideal for beginners. The bottom is sandy with scattered rocks. You'll find small fish and the occasional octopus in the rocky areas. The calm conditions make it a favourite for families with children.

Cabopino Beach

The main beach has a seagrass meadow just offshore. Seagrass is a nursery for juvenile fish and attracts rays and cuttlefish. Snorkel over the meadow slowly to spot movement. Avoid touching the seagrass as it's a protected species.

Best Time for Snorkeling

Late June to early September offers the warmest water (24-26°C) and calmest seas. May and October are also good, with water temperatures of 18-20°C. Wind conditions matter—check the forecast for levante (easterly wind) which can stir up sediment. Our skippers monitor conditions daily and will advise on the best spot for the day.

Visibility is typically best in the morning before the sea breeze picks up. Plan to arrive at your chosen cove by 10:00 for optimal conditions.

What to Bring

  • Swimwear and towel
  • Reef-safe sunscreen (to protect marine life)
  • Water shoes (for rocky entries)
  • Underwater camera or GoPro
  • A rash guard or wetsuit (optional, for cooler months)

We provide all snorkeling gear, drinks, and snacks. If you have specific dietary requirements, let us know when booking.

Other Activities Near Cabopino

After snorkeling, consider a short cruise to the Cabopino Marina for lunch at one of the seafood restaurants. Alternatively, head west to the sand dunes of Artola (a protected natural area) or east to Calahonda. Our [marbella boat rental](/blog/marbella-boat-rental-cabopino-snorkeling-spots-map/) page has more ideas for combining snorkeling with a coastal tour.

For a full day, you could visit Cabopino in the morning, then cruise to Estepona or Sotogrande for lunch. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is fast enough to cover these distances comfortably.

Frequently asked questions

How do I get to Cabopino from Marbella by boat?

Depart from Puerto Banús and head east along the coast. It's a 20-minute ride at cruising speed (15-20 knots). The marina at Cabopino is small but welcoming, with mooring buoys available.

What are the best snorkeling spots near Cabopino?

Cala del Faro offers rocky seabeds with abundant marine life. Cala Cortés has clear, shallow waters ideal for beginners. Cabopino Beach itself has seagrass meadows where you can spot octopus and sea bream.

Do I need my own snorkeling gear?

We provide masks, snorkels, and fins on request for all charters. Just let us know when booking. Life jackets are also available if you prefer extra buoyancy.

What is the best time of year for snorkeling in Cabopino?

Late June to early September offers the warmest water (24-26°C) and calmest seas. May and October are also good, but water temperatures drop to 18-20°C.

Can I anchor near the snorkeling spots?

Yes, you can anchor in sandy patches near Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés. Avoid anchoring on seagrass (Posidonia oceanica) as it's protected. Our skipper will find the best spot.

What boats are best for a snorkeling trip to Cabopino?

For a small group, the Speedboat (6.4m, 6 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are agile and easy to maneuver. For larger parties, the Azimut 39 (11 pax) or Mangusta 80 (12 pax) offer more comfort.

Is Cabopino suitable for beginners?

Absolutely. Cala Cortés has shallow, calm water with gentle entry. The seabed is sandy with some rocks, making it ideal for first-time snorkelers. Our skipper can offer tips.

What marine life can I expect to see?

Common sightings include salema, bream, damselfish, octopus, and occasionally cuttlefish. If you're lucky, you might spot a starfish or a small ray in the sandy areas.
